newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Pacific Capital to open shr offer on July 30.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Pacific Capital to open shr offer on July 30.

text.p: Pacific Capital Assets Ltd is to open a share offer July 30, with closing on August 19, despite a holdup in the consent process for its first project, Auckland's Britomart complex.
Pacific Capital said in a statement it would buy back shares if the project failed to proceed by June 30, 1998.
The offer comprises 65 million ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each, payable in two instalments.
The first NZ$0.50 instalment is payable on application, with the second falling due when called on or after May 31, 2000.

Under the buyback arrangement, Pacific Capital would repurchase partly paid ordinary shares at NZ$0.50 each if the development agreement did not become unconditional by next June, or if contracts were materially changed.

Auckland City Council on July 1 approved Britomart Investments and Britomart Developments -- both Pacific Capital units -- as development manager and developer for the site in Auckland's downtown waterfront area.

But the Auckland Regional Council has declined to give its consent for the project because the city council had not established that de-watering of the site would not result in damage to neighbouring builldings. The issue is to go before the Environment Court at an as-yet unspecified date.
Walter Bau AG, and its unit Concrete Constructions Pty Ltd, have been named as builder for stage one work.
Pacific Capital, which aims to carry out infrastructural projects throughout New Zealand, Australia and Asia, is managed by Jihong Lu, Kerry Haycock, David Atkin and Peter Cross.

The company is backed by a consortium of investors based in Australia and Asia including Hudson Corporate Pty Ltd, which is part of Hudson Timber and Hardware Ltd, Idris Hydraulic (Malaysia) Berhad and First KL Group.
